I've been farming this same plot for most of my adult life. The land here in Quzhou knows me and I know it. My two children left for the city years ago, so it's just me and my wife now. 4.1 mu is enough for us — we sell what we don't eat.

**My thinking:**

The rotation is the same as my father taught me. Wheat goes in around October after I work the soil, maize follows after the wheat harvest in June. I don't break what isn't broken.

For wheat, I use the improved seeds from the county supply cooperative — I've used them for over ten years and they outperform the old varieties. I put down base fertilizer before planting, then top-dress at jointing. I irrigate at seeding if the soil is dry, again at jointing, at heading, and once more at grain filling. Four times. That's what this land needs in a dry year. Two sprays — one herbicide early, one fungicide before heading. I rotary till before seeding.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed. After the wheat is off, I rotary till lightly and get the maize in fast — every day counts in that gap. I put more nitrogen on maize than wheat, split it: some at planting, the rest at tasseling. I irrigate at planting if soil is dry, at tasseling, and maybe once more if August is hot. Two pesticide sprays — herbicide early and one for corn borer if I see them, which I usually do.

I don't experiment at my age. I do what gives me a reliable harvest.
